Commentary.Commentary: The stage is set for the chase to begin. The Namibian openers, Louren Steenkamp and Jan Frylinck, are in the middle, and the South African fielders are positioned. Nandre Burger will bowl the first over for South Africa in this run-chase.
…THE RUN CHASE…

Chasing 135, Namibia will need a disciplined and confident batting display against a potent South African bowling lineup to pull off a memorable win. As for the Proteas, they’ll back their bowlers to defend this modest total. So, who’s your pick at the halfway mark? Stick with us, the second innings promises to be a thrilling watch!

Namibia impressed with the ball and were even sharper in the field, pulling off some outstanding catches. Ruben Trumpelmann led the bowling attack with figures of 3/28, while Max Heingo, JJ Smit, Ben Shikongo, and Gerald Erasmus all chipped in with key wickets. Special credit goes to Bernard Scholtz, who, despite going wicketless, maintained remarkable control with an economy rate of just four runs per over.

Opting to bat first on a tricky surface, South Africa huffed and puffed their way to a fighting 134/8 in 20 overs. The visitors were on the back foot early, losing Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks inside the Powerplay. A stabilizing partnership between Lhuan-dre Pretorius (22) and Rubin Hermann (23) offered some resistance, but neither could convert their starts into a substantial score. Wickets continued to fall at regular intervals, stalling any hopes of a big total. Jason Smith provided a crucial boost with a well-made 31, while a couple of late boundaries from Gerald Coetzee helped nudge the total past the 130-mark, giving South Africa something to bowl at.

Commentary.Commentary: The national anthems and pre-match formalities are over, and now it's time for the cricket action to kick off. Lhuan-dre Pretorius is opening the innings for SA along with Quinton de Kock who is returning to T20I cricket for the first time after coming out of retirement in this format. Gerhard Erasmus will be bowling the first over for Namibia.
The teams have lined up along with the match officials for the pre-match ceremonials. The national anthems are about to be played - South Africa's will be first, followed by Namibia's.
Namibia (Playing XI) - Jan Frylinck, Louren Steenkamp, Jan Nicol Loftie-Eaton, Gerhard Erasmus, JJ Smit, Malan Kruger, Ruben Trumpelmann, Zane Green(WK), Bernard Scholtz, Ben Shikongo, Max Heingo.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock(WK), Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Reeza Hendricks, Rubin Hermann, Jason Smith, Donovan Ferreira(C), Andile Simelane, Bjorn Fortuin, Gerald Coetzee, Nandre Burger, Lizaad Williams.
Toss - South Africa have won the toss and opted to BAT.

With two ambitious and well-balanced sides taking the field today, this promises to be a thrilling contest. So, who are you backing to come out on top? Let's find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly. Stay tuned!

On the other side, Namibia enters this fixture riding high on confidence, having qualified for their fourth consecutive T20 World Cup. They finished second in the Africa Region Qualifier, narrowly losing to Zimbabwe in a hard-fought final. The home team will rely on the batting firepower of JJ Smit, Jan Frylinck, Gerhard Erasmus, and Louren Steenkamp, while their bowling attack will be spearheaded by Ben Shikongo, Jan Nicol Loftie-Eaton, Bernard Scholtz, and the ever-reliable Ruben Trumpelmann to get a win against the Proteas side.

For South Africa, Donovan Ferreira takes on captaincy duties for the first time, while Quinton de Kock makes a return to the national side, coming out of retirement for the limited-overs format. The batting unit will depend on Reeza Hendricks, Rubin Hermann, and Lhuan-dre Pretorius. Meanwhile, the bowling attack features the likes of Nandre Burger, Gerald Coetzee, and Ottniel Baartman, who will play pivotal roles. With the T20 World Cup just months away, the Proteas will be keen to fine-tune their combinations and identify key players for the global tournament.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the one-off T20 International between Namibia and South Africa, from the Namibia Cricket Ground in Windhoek. It’s a historic day for Namibian cricket as this marks the official opening of their first international-standard stadium, and fittingly, it plays host to the very first international match between these two African nations
…MATCHDAY…

They say firsts are always special, but in cricket, they become moments that shape history and define what follows. With more associate nations gaining international exposure, each contest offers a chance to grow, to compete, and to test their strengths against formidable opposition. This occasion carries that same sense of significance. For the first time in any format, Namibia and South Africa will meet, with the Namibia Cricket Ground in Windhoek setting the stage for a one-off T20I that promises both meaning and excitement. What began as cricket under the name South West Africa in the early 1960s later evolved into Namibia stepping firmly onto the international stage. From the 1961-62 season, South West Africa competed in South African domestic country district tournaments. Following Namibia’s independence, the Namibia Cricket Board was formed in 1989 and the country became an associate member of the ICC in 1992. Currently placed 16th in the ICC T20I rankings, Namibia has already secured its spot in the 2026 T20 World Cup. Riding on that momentum, Gerhard Erasmus’ side will be eager to make a statement and show that they can compete at the highest level, aiming to challenge the mighty South Africans in home conditions. JJ Smit and Jan Frylinck have been the standout performers with the bat this year, while Ruben Trumpelmann, Ben Shikongo, and Bernard Scholtz, have impressed with their bowling, giving Namibia a well-rounded attack heading into the contest. Led by the in-form Donovan Ferreira, South Africa arrive with a second-string squad that still features experienced campaigners like Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks in the batting line-up, alongside the likes of Bjorn Fortuin in the bowling department. Beyond these names, it is a youthful side, with Lhuan-dre Pretorius eager to make a mark with the bat. The bowling unit looks formidable even in Rabada’s absence, with the pace trio of Gerald Coetzee, Nandre Burger, and Lizaad Williams serving as their primary strike weapons, while Nqabayomzi Peter and Fortuin marshal the spin attack. The absence of Kwena Maphaka, however, is a significant setback to an already potent bowling weaponry. It takes barely two and a half hours to fly from Cape Town to Windhoek, yet it has taken decades for cricketing ties between these two nations to come to fruition. This encounter is therefore more than just a match, but it is a celebration of Namibia’s long journey in cricket. Now, all eyes will be on whether the hosts can rise to challenge the mighty Proteas.
